reports.name: AAFC Outlook for Principal Field Crops (Canada)

outlook: Grains were mostly a little firmer in Tuesday's overnight trade after Monday's losses. December corn was up half a cent near $4.67 after closing Monday below its October WASDE low on harvest hedging, and November soybeans were up 4 cents near $12.57 as USDA confirmed another 114,000 tonnes sold to China, bringing four days of sales to about 1.47 million tonnes. Monday's Crop Progress put soybean harvest at 64% (behind trade expectations), corn harvest around 44% (about 5 points behind average) and winter wheat planting at 63%, 6 points behind average. Chicago December wheat was up about 4 cents near $6.60 on Black Sea shipping risks and higher crude oil, while Minneapolis December spring wheat was flat near $6.70 and ICE canola held near C$788 per tonne.

news.title: Conflicts driving wheat prices and some 2027 acreage decisions
